title: MySQL / InnoDB
workload: Relational OLTP, similar placement to PostgreSQL, with a large existing operational ecosystem and group-replication / InnoDB cluster options.
consistency: Single-primary or group replication depending on deployment. Replicas lag. Do not treat 'semi-sync' as lossless without naming acknowledgements.
durability: InnoDB redo + binlog. Crash recovery is not the same as replica promotion safety.
latency: Indexed PK lookups in-region are low ms; binlog apply lag is the replica story.
failure: Primary death needs fencing. GTID/binlog position is a timeline; dual writers corrupt replicas.
whenToChoose: SQL + transactions when the organization already operates MySQL well, or you need a specific MySQL ecosystem feature.
whenNot: When you needed Dynamo-style item scale or Cassandra multi-master ingest. Failover slogans without fencing still split-brain.

title: MongoDB
workload: Document access with secondary indexes, aggregation, and replica-set HA. Flexible schema is not a substitute for access-pattern design.
consistency: Primary reads by default in a replica set. Secondary reads are lagged. Majority write concern is not linearizability of all reads.
durability: WiredTiger + majority journal to a voting majority when you ask for it. w:1 can lose acknowledged writes on failover.
latency: Good for targeted document reads; unindexed scans and large documents dominate tails.
failure: Replica-set election in seconds. Rollback of w:1 writes is possible. Shard cluster failures are independent per shard.
whenToChoose: Document model that matches how you read, with replica-set majority writes for durable OLTP.
whenNot: Multi-document transactions as a default across shards, or treating the cluster as a cache. Not a drop-in for SQL constraints.

title: Apache Cassandra
workload: High-ingest wide rows and query tables. Availability-oriented writes with tunable per-request consistency.
consistency: ONE/QUORUM/ALL. QUORUM ≠ linearizable. Repairs reconcile later. LWW and tombstones are part of the model.
durability: Commitlog + SSTables. Hinted handoff is not a substitute for repair.
latency: Strong ingest p50; compaction/GC tails. LOCAL_QUORUM vs cross-DC ALL changes the budget.
failure: Node loss expected. ALL becomes unavailable. Wrong gc_grace can resurrect deletes.
whenToChoose: When write availability and pre-modeled query tables beat ad-hoc SQL, and you will staff repair.
whenNot: TokenX-style constrained multi-row ledgers, small teams, or 'just use QUORUM' as a correctness slogan.

title: OpenSearch
workload: Full-text search, logs, and analytics on derived documents. Near-real-time index, not an OLTP primary.
consistency: Refresh interval, not commit. Search hits can miss recent primary writes and can include later-deleted docs until refresh.
durability: Primary + replica shards. Still rebuildable from the source of truth.
latency: Query latency depends on heap, shard count, and aggregations. Refresh is a visibility delay, not durability.
failure: Yellow/red clusters, split-brain if discovery is wrong, mapping explosions, ingest backlog.
whenToChoose: Search and log analytics beside a real primary. Reindex is an allowed recovery.
whenNot: Spendable balances, unique allocation, or any authority that cannot be rebuilt. Never treat _id hits as the ledger.

title: Object storage (S3-class)
workload: Immutable or versioned blobs, backups, data lake files. Metadata catalog usually lives in a database.
consistency: Same-region object CRUD and LIST are strongly consistent. Cross-region replication still lags. Not a row store.
durability: Storage class and cross-region replication settings. 'Eleven nines' marketing is not a restore time.
latency: PUT/GET in tens to hundreds of ms plus TTFB for large objects. Multipart for large files.
failure: Slow PUT, incomplete multipart, Glacier restore delay, or permission/KMS outages.
whenToChoose: Large binary objects and backup archives. Pair with a DB for the catalog and authz.
whenNot: Low-latency item mutations, compare-and-swap ledgers, or listing-as-query. Object storage is not PostgreSQL.

title: Envoy / L7 proxy
workload: L7 proxy for HTTP/gRPC, retries, outlier detection, and mesh data plane.
consistency: Retry and timeout policies can duplicate writes. Membership is derived from xDS.
latency: Extra hop; connection pooling reduces handshake tails.
failure: Sidecar/process death blackholes the listener. Retry storms under 5xx.
whenToChoose: When you need consistent L7 policy beside app code.
whenNot: Auto-retry of non-idempotent TokenX POSTs, or treating the proxy as a ledger.

title: Apache Kafka
workload: Partitioned durable log for pub/sub and replay.
consistency: Per-partition order. No global order. ISR defines who may be elected.
durability: acks=all + minISR is the produce story you must name. Retention bounds replay.
latency: Produce p99 depends on ISR and disk. Consume lag is a different SLO.
failure: Controller, disk, ISR shrink, consumer rebalance. Not an instantaneous, lossless cutover.
whenToChoose: When replay and fan-out from a log beat ad-hoc queues.
whenNot: As a TokenX uniqueness store without a sink constraint, or as a request-response database.

title: CDN (CloudFront-class)
workload: Derived GET cache at the edge. TLS termination optional.
consistency: TTL / versioned objects. Invalidation is best-effort fan-out, not a transaction.
latency: Hit TTFB low tens of ms globally; miss is origin + extra hop.
failure: Stale-if-error is a product choice. Origin death with empty edge is still an outage for uncached objects.
whenNot: Private per-user balances, POSTs, or as the source of truth.

title: etcd / Raft lease service
workload: Small linearizable KV, elections, Kubernetes membership.
consistency: Linearizable reads through the protocol you enable. Leases expire.
durability: Majority of the Raft group. Keep the dataset small.
latency: Majority RTT. Cross-region majority is expensive.
failure: Leader election. Split votes. Using it as an application database overloads the cluster.
whenNot: Click firehose, user content, or TokenX balances at payment QPS.
